### security.security.current_user

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** `anonymous` · **Readers:** `["anonymous"]`

Retrieve the system metadata for the currently logged in user

*(inferred)* Looks up the caller's session in the live session table and returns a copy of that session's user object with `sessionid` added.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | This request metadata is automatically provided by the Newbound framework. Pass a placeholder value like null when calling it from javascript. |

**HTTP:** `GET /security/current_user`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies \
  "http://localhost:8080/security/current_user"
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"security","cmd":"current_user","params":{}}
```

**MCP tool:** `security-security-current_user`

**See also:** [deleteuser](#securitysecuritydeleteuser), [groups](#securitysecuritygroups), [init](#securitysecurityinit), [setuser](#securitysecuritysetuser), [users](#securitysecurityusers)

### security.security.deleteuser

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Deletes a user from the system using their unique identifier, returning "OK" on successful removal.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | yes | The ID of the user to delete |

**HTTP:** `GET /security/deleteuser`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/security/deleteuser" \
  --data-urlencode 'id=<id>'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text

```

**MCP tool:** `security-security-deleteuser`

### security.security.init

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Initializes the application's core security and user management, loading existing user data and establishing a default administrator if none exists. It then starts a background process responsible for continuously monitoring and expiring inactive user sessions. The command returns an empty JSON object upon successful initialization.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /security/init`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies \
  "http://localhost:8080/security/init"
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"security","cmd":"init","params":{}}
```

### security.security.setuser

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Creates a new user or updates an existing one, returning the complete user record as a JSONObject. Takes the String `id` (the account's primary key), the String `displayname`, the String `password`, and a JSONArray `groups` of group names; plus `keepalive`, `address` and `port` (Any), each stored only when its string form is not "null", so a null leaves that property unset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | yes | The unique identifier for the user account, serving as the primary key for retrieving and storing user data. |
| `displayname` | String | yes | The user's human-readable name, used for display purposes rather than identification. |
| `password` | String | yes | The user's authentication password. This string value is stored for verifying user identity during login. |
| `groups` | JSONArray | yes | A JSON array specifying the groups a user belongs to, with each element being a string identifier for a particular group. |
| `keepalive` | Any | no | Indicates whether the user's connection or session should be kept alive. This setting is activated when its string representation evaluates to "true". |
| `address` | Any | no | Network address to associate with the account; stored only when its string form is not "null". Pass null when not applicable — the param is still required. |
| `port` | Any | no | Network port to associate with the account; stored as both "port" and "p2pport" when its string form is not "null". Pass null when not applicable — the param is still required. |

**HTTP:** `GET /security/setuser`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/security/setuser" \
  --data-urlencode 'id=<id>' \
  --data-urlencode 'displayname=<displayname>' \
  --data-urlencode 'password=<password>' \
  --data-urlencode 'groups=[]'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"security","cmd":"setuser","params":{"id":"<id>","displayname":"<displayname>","password":"<password>","groups":[]}}
```

**MCP tool:** `security-security-setuser`

**See also:** [current_user](#securitysecuritycurrent_user), [deleteuser](#securitysecuritydeleteuser), [groups](#securitysecuritygroups), [init](#securitysecurityinit), [users](#securitysecurityusers)
